ota.playerApkSubtitle: Download the Android kiosk build and decide whether paired screens auto-update.
ota.autoUpdateOnDesc: Paired kiosks pull new APK builds on their 6-hour cadence — hands-off but a buggy release can break working screens.
ota.autoUpdateOffDesc: Kiosks stay pinned at their current APK version. Admins push updates per-screen via the gear icon on each screen card.
ota.installWindowDesc: When set, dashboard "Push update" still works — but the install only APPLIES during this daily window in the configured timezone. Downloads happen anytime in the background (no disruption). Use this to keep customer-facing screens uninterrupted during business hours.
ota.wraparoundSuffix: means "10 PM to 4 AM next day"). Per-push override available on the screen Push dialog.
ota.canaryDesc: Lower the percentage to stage a release. Only the hashed cohort of screens (deterministic from screen ID, never re-rolled) receives the new APK; the rest stay on their current version. After the soak window elapses without any install errors in the cohort, auto-promote bumps back to 100%.
ota.canaryHelp: Use 5–10% for a risky release; 25–50% for routine updates. Set to 0 to pause OTA entirely (e.g. during finals week).

display.notReported: This screen hasn’t reported what it can control yet. The player checks its own hardware at startup and sends the result on its next check-in — controls appear here automatically once it does. Browser-based players never report and cannot be controlled remotely.

display.notDelivered: Not delivered — the server accepted the command but couldn’t reach this screen’s live connection. Nothing changed on the screen. Try again in a moment; if it keeps failing, check that the screen is online.
display.noPushSocket: This screen has no live connection right now, so an instant command has no way down to it — nothing changed on the screen, and display commands aren’t queued for later. It usually reconnects on its own within a few minutes; try again then. If it stays this way, the venue network is most likely blocking realtime connections.

note.volumeNone: This device exposes no volume interface — nothing here can change its audio level.
note.brightnessSysfs: Real backlight control — lower settings actually save power.
note.brightnessSettings: Dims the picture in software — this panel’s backlight can’t be set remotely.
note.brightnessSoftware: Dims the image only — this box exposes no backlight control, so the panel keeps drawing full power.
note.blankSoftware: Covers the screen with black — this box exposes no true screen-off, so the backlight stays lit.
note.rebootBlockedOtherOwner: Not available — another management app already owns this device, so remote restart can’t be granted.
note.rebootNeedsProvisioning: Not available — remote restart needs device-owner setup, which means a factory reset and re-enrolling this box.
note.rebootUnavailable: Not available — this device hasn’t granted remote restart.
note.blankDeviceAdmin: Should turn the screen off. This box reports a device-admin app is active — if that admin isn’t our player, it falls back to covering the screen with black and the backlight stays lit.
note.blankVendorRecipe: Uses this manufacturer’s own power command, which on most panels is a real screen-off. If the command turns out to be wrong for this model, the player falls back to covering the screen with black.
note.blankScreenTimeout: Uses the Android screen timeout to power the panel down. Most signage boxes honour it; a few ignore it and just show black.
note.blankNotReported: Not available yet — until this screen says whether it can power its panel off, blanking stays off until it does. Wake and raising the brightness still work.
note.wakeNotReported: Wake always works, even before a screen reports: it can only ever make a dark screen visible.
note.brightnessVendorRecipe: Uses this manufacturer’s own backlight command — lower settings actually save power.
note.brightnessRecoveryOnly: Until this screen reports what it can control, brightness can only be RAISED (never below {min}%) — we don’t darken hardware we haven’t seen.

streamingSso.bridgeCaptureExplain: We capture the HDMI output of {provider}'s player and stream it into VenueOS as a regular channel, so it shows up in our templates with overlays, ad slots, schedules, and emergency takeover just like any other source.
streamingSso.bridgeStepsPending: Bridge setup steps are still being authored for this provider. In the meantime, the general workflow is: HDMI output → USB capture card → mini-PC running ffmpeg → local HLS URL. Reach out to support and we'll walk you through it.

streamingSso.noCmsCanPlay: No signage CMS can play Hulu, Netflix, Disney+, Max, Peacock, Paramount+, fuboTV, or Sling directly.
streamingSso.notVenueosLimitation: That's not a VenueOS limitation — none of our competitors (Yodeck, Rise Vision, OptiSigns, ScreenCloud, BrightSign) can either. Three reasons:
streamingSso.noPublicApiDetail: These services don't publish a way for third-party apps to authenticate and play their content. Their apps only run on licensed devices (Roku, Fire TV, Apple TV, Smart TVs).
streamingSso.drmDetail: Their video files are encrypted with DRM that requires a hardware-backed license. Browser-based players in a CMS don't have those licenses.
streamingSso.commercialForbiddenDetail: Even if you could technically embed their video, their consumer Terms of Service explicitly prohibit displaying it in commercial venues. That's a contract problem, not a tech problem.
streamingSso.bridgeExplainDetail: You keep your existing Hulu / Netflix subscription on a $50 Fire TV Stick. We capture its HDMI output through a $180 USB capture card, encode to HLS on a $170 mini-PC, and play that HLS stream inside VenueOS like any other channel.
streamingSso.bridgeWorksAll: The same bridge works for every closed platform: DIRECTV for Business, DISH, Atmosphere TV, Mood Media, Stingray (iHeart for Business). Setup takes about 30 minutes — we ship a step-by-step wizard.
streamingSso.whatWorksNoBridge: What works without a bridge today

streamingSso.soundtrackFinalizing: We're finalizing our Soundtrack Your Brand OAuth integration. While the partner approval clears, your account can be activated manually by our sales team — typical turnaround is 1-2 business days.
streamingSso.soundtrackProvisionByHand: and we'll provision your Soundtrack account by hand. Once OAuth ships, your existing connection migrates automatically — no re-pair required.
